title: どうしても — no matter what, absolutely
summary: An adverb that stresses strong will or impossibility: “no matter what.” With a wish (～たい), it means “I absolutely want to.” With a negative (～ない), it means “I just can't, however I try.”

patterns.form: どうしても ＋ 〜たい／〜なければならない
patterns.gloss: strong wish or need: どうしても入りたい

patterns.form: どうしても ＋ 〜ない／〜わけにはいかない
patterns.gloss: can't, however I try: どうしても思い出せない

body.p: With a positive wish or need, どうしても means “whatever it takes”: どうしてもこの大学に入りたい. With a negative or impossible meaning, it means “however hard I try, it does not work”: どうしても思い出せない (I simply can't remember).

body.h: Do not confuse with どうして
body.p: どうして (without も) means “why”. どうしても is a different expression about strong will or impossibility. Also, ～わけにはいかない after どうしても means “there is no way I can ～”: 休むわけにはいかない.

examples.ja: どうしてもこの大学（だいがく）に入（はい）りたい。
examples.tr: I want to get into this university no matter what.

examples.ja: どうしてもその漢字（かんじ）が思（おも）い出（だ）せない。
examples.tr: No matter what I do, I simply can't remember that kanji.

examples.ja: 明日（あした）はどうしても休（やす）むわけにはいかない。
examples.romaji: Ashita wa dōshitemo yasumu wake ni wa ikanai.
examples.tr: There is absolutely no way I can take tomorrow off.

pitfalls: Do not mix it up with どうして (why). The も changes the meaning completely.
Match the second half to the meaning: a wish or duty for “absolutely”, a negative for “can't”.
